questions.question: On a leaf spring, what should be true?
questions.explanation: Check leaf springs during vehicle inspection. Make sure no leaves are missing or broken. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: If you start a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, what may happen?

options.text: Will likely complete the turn satisfactorily.
May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Can expect other drivers to move their vehicles to accommodate your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: May hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, is it important to know what is happening behind you?
questions.explanation: You should always be aware of what is happening behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder regularly.

questions.question: When driving in fog and you see taillights ahead, what should you know?

options.text: The lights may not indicate where the road is as the vehicle may have pulled off the roadway.
You can assume the vehicle ahead is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not indicate where the road is as the vehicle may have pulled off the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, do not trust lights to show you where the road is. A vehicle's lights may come from a car that has pulled off the road.

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
No sooner than the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No sooner than the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. Turning too early can cause the left side of your vehicle to hit another vehicle.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, stay away from them. Keep a safe distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: A check of the engine oil level.

questions.correctAnswerText: A check of the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the engine oil level, coolant level, and the condition of hoses.

questions.question: What does rough acceleration do to a vehicle?

options.text: Is common if a vehicle is warmed up.
Is encouraged to improve gas mileage.

questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can harm your vehicle.

questions.question: What is a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces called?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road underneath shows through it, so it looks like a wet road. Be very careful when it is below freezing and the road appears wet.

questions.question: When checking tires, which should not cause concern?

options.text: Tread of at least 4/32 of an inch on front tires
Radial and bias-ply tires used together

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread of at least 4/32 of an inch on front tires
questions.explanation: Front tires should have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Other tires should have at least 2/32 of an inch. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires, and do not use tires of different sizes.

questions.question: Why is rolling backward when you start to accelerate dangerous?

options.text: The truck is not made to go backwards.
You may hit a vehicle behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit a vehicle behind you.
questions.explanation: Make sure you can accelerate without rolling back first. Rolling backwards can cause you to hit a vehicle or obstacle behind your truck.

questions.question: What should you know about people working on a disabled vehicle?

options.text: They are aware of the roadway.
They may be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
They do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be focused on the repair and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive carefully near people working on a disabled vehicle on the roadside. They may be focused on fixing the vehicle and not paying attention to traffic around them.

questions.question: When you check windshield wiper blades, what should they be?
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage, hard rubber, and that they are tight. Clean the blades if they are dirty.

questions.question: When you stop, how should you press the brake pedal?
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: What happens when you travel downhill?

options.text: Your vehicle travels at the same speed as on flat road.

questions.explanation: Gravity makes your vehicle go faster when traveling downhill. Slow down before you reach a downhill slope.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Instead, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch. This helps you get traction back.

questions.question: When are you most likely to hit strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. You are especially likely to hit strong winds when exiting a tunnel.

questions.question: What should a driver do after arriving at a destination?

options.text: Tell passengers to take their belongings when they leave.
Only announce this after passengers start to exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell passengers to take their belongings when they leave.
questions.explanation: When you reach a destination or stop, remind passengers to take their belongings before exiting. Make this announcement before the bus stops completely.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms muscle control, reaction time, sight, and judgment. For some people, one drink can cause impairment. Do not drive after any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When driving on a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Slow down when the road is wet because tires have less grip. Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads.
